title: Long-form Illustrated History Baseline

composition: Alternate maps, character tableaux, artifacts, and expressive close-ups.
Use foreground, midground, and background layers for economical parallax.
Give each historical proposition one dominant visual subject.
Let recurring environments and character silhouettes preserve chronology.
motion_economics: Favor cutout pose changes, prop swaps, camera pushes, and parallax over continuous character animation.
Increase overlapping motion and atmospheric layers only when historical complexity increases.
Use a held consequence pose after a comic or consequential action.

patterns: Map pan or zoom into a character, place, or artifact.
Hard-cut to a short reaction gag after a dense factual sentence.
Use page, smoke, geography, or object-shape transitions between related ideas.
Reset chapters with a title card or a materially different scale.

visual_hierarchy: Thick dark outlines contain flat earthy color fields.
Warm historical environments carry muted green, tan, cream, red, and blue roles.
Faces and props carry the joke; maps and documents carry chronology.
sound_hierarchy: Narration remains dominant over restrained music.
Paper, map, prop, and environmental cues make limited animation feel intentional.
Short comic punctuations and selective cinematic impacts mark consequences.

reserved_identity: Exact character designs, silhouettes, facial constructions, and recurring cast
Exact palette values, textures, backgrounds, maps, props, and source frames
Logos, typography treatments, title cards, catchphrases, scripts, and jokes
Shot-for-shot recreation or tracing of any studied work
